transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my breathing, mostly. I get out of breath climbing the stairs at home, and it's been getting worse over about the last three months.
When did you first notice it?
I'd say about three months ago it started, and it's crept up on me gradually since then. There wasn't one particular day.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It comes on when I climb the stairs or walk uphill, and it settles down if I rest for two or three minutes. Otherwise, when I'm sitting, I'm fine.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
I'd say I'm puffed out — I have to stop and catch my breath. It's not painful, just that I can't get enough air in when I'm exerting myself.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's not in one spot — it's just a general feeling of being short of breath all over, really. It doesn't spread anywhere, and there's no pain with it.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
When it's at its worst, on the stairs, I'd call it a 6 or 7. I have to stop halfway up our 14 stairs to get my breath, whereas I used to manage the whole flight without stopping.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — only with exertion. When I'm sitting down or resting I'm not breathless at all.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Well, my ankles are a bit puffy by the evening, and I've started using two pillows at night instead of one. Other than that, no chest pain, no cough, and no fever.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I have a few things. I've had atrial fibrillation for about five years now, and I had a heart attack twelve years ago.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?
I take four: rivaroxaban 15 mg once a day with my evening meal, bisoprolol 5 mg once a day, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and ramipril 2.5 mg once a day. No new ones.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, no known drug allergies that I'm aware of.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Yes, it's slowing me down. I have to stop halfway up the stairs, which I never used to, and I'm a bit wary about managing them to get to bed. It's on my mind.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes — two things really. I'm worried about how I'll manage the stairs to get to bed, and I'd like to know whether my heart is getting worse.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
